text:
maria: Heads-up — PR #6402 (pareto-aware scheduler) canary showed a 18% bump in p95 for long-seq workloads. attaching quick numbers and a short repro.

dave: Ugh, thanks for flagging. Is this from the nightly canary or a manual bench?

maria: nightly canary on canary-cluster-3. Raw jenkins job: `bench/latency-longseq --runs=30 --model=gptx-13b --tokens=2048`
Results (median over runs): p50 42ms -> 44ms, p95 212ms -> 250ms, p99 410ms -> 430ms. baseline -> pr-6402.

josh: 38–odd ms to 44ms is fine, but p95 212 -> 250 is not. Do you have allocation/placement traces? could be bin-packing change.

maria: attaching snippet of the canary logs below. looked like more microbatch spillovers in the middle of sequences.
```
[2029-07-12T03:12:10Z] trace_id=abc123 schedule: node-a->node-b swap, microbatch_size 8 -> 16 midstream
[2029-07-12T03:12:11Z] kv_cache_miss_rate +12%
[2029-07-12T03:12:11Z] latency-spike p95 260ms
```

sam: @dave @josh can you triage whether this is scheduler logic regressing or an interaction with allocation heuristics? If it's scheduler, we should hold the merge.

dave: I'll run a focused bench comparing placement policy old vs new. will post a narrow repro with a deterministic config. ETA ~2h.

kat: pinging infra — if this is allocation-related, we should check if the autoscaler triggered extra pods mid-run. ci-bot, did autoscaler fire during that canary window?

ci-bot: canary-run 1876504000: autoscaler scaled up 2 -> 4 nodes at 03:11:40Z; reason: sustained queue growth > 120s.

josh: autoscaler scale-up during the run would explain mid-run microbatch expansion. that'd cause p95 tail. we should confirm if the PR changed any batching thresholds that make queues grow earlier.

maria: PR diff snippet that touches scheduling thresholds: `scheduler/batching.go` lines 120-140, changed target_utilization from 0.72 -> 0.78. full link: https://git.redwood/6402/files

sam: increasing target_utilization could push load higher before scaling; combined with a small bug in placement -> tail. if we revert that parameter only, maybe merge can go through.

dave: local repro started. early numbers look consistent: with old util target p95 218ms, with new target p95 248ms. I'll run with autoscaler disabled to isolate.

maria: thanks. for process: I'd suggest we hold the merge for now and open a follow-up PR to tune util target + add a canary test that blocks on p95 > 220ms for long-seq. thoughts?

kat: agree on a hold. we should also add tracepoint logs around microbatch changes so these spikes are easier to attribute.

josh: I'll prepare a tiny revert PR that only rolls back the threshold change and add a targeted e2e test. can we get 1 approval from runtime owners to proceed with revert?

sam: @dave @maria can approve once dave confirms isolation results. @maria please mark the PR as hold and add the canary link.

maria: done — PR marked `hold: performance-regression`. added canary job link and raw logs. https://ci.redwood/canary/1876504000

dave: isolation complete — with autoscaler locked, p95 difference shrinks to 6%, but still ~13ms. looks like both autoscaler timing + scheduler util change contribute.

josh: sounds like we should revert the util bump and follow up with a better autoscaler smoothing/lead-time fix.

sam: Agreed. @josh please open the revert PR and tag runtime leads, and @maria please add a post-merge regression guard (canary alert) to catch similar shifts.

maria: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
